5.0.0.en: 1 “Hear ye this, O priests! and hearken, ye house of Israel! and give ye ear, O house of the king! for judgment is toward you, because ye have been a snare on Mizpah, and a net spread upon Tabor. 2 And they have gone deep into the sacrifices of deviation, and I am a chastisement to them all. 3 I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hid from me: for now, O Ephraim, thou committest whoredom, and Israel is defiled. 4 Their doings will not suffer them to turn unto their God: for the spirit of whoredoms is in the midst of them, and they have not known the LORD. 5 And the pride of Israel is humbled in his face: therefore shall Israel and Ephraim fall in their iniquity; Judah also shall fall with them.”

5.1.0.en: God affirms that He shows no partiality to one group at the expense of another, or to one person at the expense of another, but since all have sinned He disciplines all, saying: “I am a chastisement to them all” [2]. He disciplines Israel because it began the evil and set up for itself a temple other than the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem and turned aside to idolatry; and at the same time He also disciplines Judah, despite the privileges it bore, since its capital is Jerusalem and within it is the temple of the Lord, and it is a royal tribe, but since it sinned, even if late, it is punished: “therefore shall Israel and Ephraim fall in their iniquity; Judah also shall fall with them” [5].

5.1.1.en: If in the previous chapter a trial was announced particularly against the priests, since the people of God perished through lack of knowledge, a matter which is at the very heart of the priests’ responsibility, yet this does not excuse the people, for He says: “Hear ye this, O priests! and hearken, ye house of Israel!” [1], and He includes with them the people of dignities: “and give ye ear, O house of the king! for judgment is toward you” [1].

5.2.0.en: He condemns all, for He is the Searcher of all and nothing is hidden from Him: “I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hid from me” [3]. He mentioned Ephraim first either in the sense of the kingdom of Israel, or because Ephraim was the chief of the rebels and through him the rest of the ten tribes were defiled; therefore he mentioned him first, since he deserves discipline more than others.

5.2.1.en: What does God know about them?

5.2.2.en: First: “ye have been a snare on Mizpah, and a net spread upon Tabor” [1]. Perhaps he addresses here the leaders who ought to have supported the weak lest they fall, and behold, they became snares and nets which the enemy sets to catch every soul for the account of evil. Instead of guiding them to repentance they entice them to fall and draw them by every device to pagan worship. Some think that it was their custom to station spies on the roads, especially on the two mountains “Mizpah and Tabor,” in the days of the feasts, to watch those going to Jerusalem and report on them so that they might be tried.

5.2.3.en: It is not known whether he means here the Mizpah which is in Gilead (Judg 11:21), which is said to be the place of the heap of stones which Jacob and the people of Laban set up as a witness to the covenant made between them (Gen 31:49), and there the children of Israel gathered to fight the Ammonites (Judg 10:17), and Jephthah met his daughter (Judg 11:34), and perhaps its location was Tell Ramith; or whether it is the Mizpah which is in Benjamin where Saul was chosen king (1 Sam 10:17, 21), and which Asa fortified (1 Kgs 15:22), and where Gedaliah was killed (2 Kgs 25:23, 25), and it is said that it was the village of the prophet Samuel. In any case Mizpah and Mount Tabor were at that time two important centers of pagan worship, and they became symbols of the ruin that came because of pagan worship.

5.3.0.en: Second: their insistence on committing sin without repentance, because it springs from their depths, and because of their not knowing the Lord. “Their doings will not suffer them to turn unto their God: for the spirit of whoredoms is within them (in the midst of them), and they have not known the LORD” [4]. They are stubborn, insisting on turning away from God in ignorance.

5.4.0.en: Third: their haughtiness, or the pride of their heart, makes them despise the words of the Lord on the lips of the prophets, for He says: “And the pride of Israel is humbled in his face” [5]. “Indeed pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. Better it is to be of an humble spirit with the meek, than to divide the spoil with the proud” (Prov 16:18-19). The Lord declared His hatred of man’s pride: “The Lord GOD hath sworn by himself, saith the LORD the God of hosts, I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces: therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein” (Amos 6:8). And He says: “Thus will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem. This people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the stubbornness of their heart” (Jer 13:9-10).

5.5.0.en: 6 “They shall go with their flocks and with their herds to seek the LORD; but they shall not find him; he hath withdrawn himself from them. 7 They have dealt treacherously against the LORD: for they have begotten strange children: now shall a month devour them with their portions.”

5.5.1.en: In the pride of their hearts and their ignorance they thought they could appease God with material offerings and sacrifices without changing their hearts; therefore He says: “They shall go with their flocks and with their herds to seek the LORD; but they shall not find him; he hath withdrawn himself from them” [6]. The secret of His withdrawing from them is that they approach Him but not with their heart, therefore they do not find Him, for He is found only by the heart and seen only by it: “Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God” (Mt 5:8).

5.6.0.en: If He withdrew from them, it is because they dealt treacherously with Him, they broke the covenant made between Him and them, and instead of being united to Him to bring forth the fruit of the Spirit that gladdens the heart of God, they were united to evil and brought forth strange children, that is, fruits foreign to God… “They have dealt treacherously against the LORD: for they have begotten strange children” [7].

5.6.1.en: He concludes his saying thus: “now shall a month devour them with their portions” [7]. Perhaps he meant that at the monthly feast (the new moon), instead of rejoicing and being glad in the Lord and being satisfied with the spiritual fruit as the Lord rejoices in them, behold, they practice the ritual of the feast, but in it they lose everything, even their possessions (their portions); and perhaps by their portions which they lose he meant the defiled tables which they set up in celebration of Baal, for these became their portion instead of God Himself and His Kingdom being their portion, and this portion which they chose they lose because it is transient.

5.7.s.en: 3. Announcement of a general state of discipline

5.7.0.en: 8 “Blow ye the trumpet in Gibeah, the horn in Ramah. Cry aloud at Beth-aven: after thee, O Benjamin. 9 Ephraim shall be desolate in the day of chastisement. Among the tribes of Israel have I made known that which is sure. 10 The princes of Judah are like them that remove the bound: therefore I will pour out my wrath upon them like water. 11 Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, because he willingly walked after the commandment. 12 Therefore am I unto Ephraim as a moth, and to the house of Judah as the woodworm.”

5.7.1.en: God asks for the blowing of trumpets in both kingdoms, Israel and Judah, which are used in wars; as though God wanted to declare to them what sin does to them, for it makes the God who loves mankind appear as an enemy of theirs who fights them. In any case He asked for the blowing of the trumpets in Gibeah and the horn in Ramah, and He asked them to cry aloud at Beth-aven.

5.7.2.en: “Gibeah” means (hill), and the horn signifies power, while Ramah means (high place), as though God asks for the blowing of the trumpets on the hill in a very high place where they think they are strong, so that they may realize they are in a state of war… They accepted pagan worship and so entered into enmity with God, and behold, He permits them to be disciplined through the raids of enemies, worshipers of Baal, who attack them and plunder them of everything and take them captive. They loved Baal and his feasts and pleasures, so let them accept slavery to the people of Baal and the worshipers of strangers!

5.7.3.en: It is said that Gibeah is very close to Ramah, the first on the border of the kingdom of Judah, and the second in Israel, as though ruin comes upon both kingdoms because both have been corrupted. As for “Beth-aven” or (house of vanity)… there is no need to blow the trumpet in it, for it has utterly declined and fallen without hope, and nothing is heard in it but cries of defeat since the enemy has seized it.

5.7.4.en: He continues his speech: “after thee, O Benjamin” [8], and in some translations “Be terrified, O Benjamin.” Since the enemy has seized the hill country of Ephraim and come very near the border of Benjamin, there is no need to blow the trumpet in Benjamin, but it is enough to look behind to make souls tremble, and let them repent and return to the Lord so that what befell Ephraim may not befall them.

5.8.0.en: He continues his speech: “Among the tribes of Israel have I made known that which is sure. The princes of Judah are like them that remove the bound: therefore I will pour out my wrath upon them like water” [9-10]. God has declared in the kingdom of Israel what is sure, that is, the certain discipline that must come upon them, and not, as they thought, mere threats without action. As for the princes of Judah, God pours out upon them and the kingdom of Baal. They lost the spirit of discernment, “who distinguishes between the Egyptians (symbolically),” for nothing grieves the heart of God like the spiritual leaders’ losing the spirit of discernment, the spirit which every believer ought to carry within him.

5.8.1.en: Perhaps removing the bound also means seizure or greed; therefore the commandment came: “Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour’s landmark, which they of old time have set in thine inheritance, which thou shalt inherit in the land that the LORD thy God giveth thee to possess it” (Deut 19:14), so that a tribe may not go beyond the borders of its land but keep to the borders that God gave it.

5.9.0.en: “Ephraim is oppressed (under pressure), crushed in judgment, because he willingly walked after the commandment. Therefore am I unto Ephraim as a moth, and to the house of Judah as the woodworm” [11-12].

5.9.1.en: Ephraim fell under pressure until he was utterly crushed, so that there was no breath of life left in him; he also lost his strength, his privileges, and his rights because he agreed to walk after the commandment of Jeroboam, and of the kings after him, who compelled their subjects to the vain worship of Baal. Therefore the word “commandment” came in the Septuagint as “vanity,” that is, Ephraim agreed to walk after vanity instead of the commandment of God, which is the truth. This conduct causes them to lose the enjoyment of God’s blessings in their lives, and God becomes to them like the moth that spoils the garment, so that their nakedness and shame are exposed, and God will be to Judah also like the woodworm that destroys wood or the beams of a house, so that the house collapses and Judah is left without shelter.

5.10.0.en: 13 “When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah saw his wound, then went Ephraim to Assyria, and sent to an enemy king: yet could he not heal you, nor cure you of your wound. 14 For I will be unto Ephraim as a lion, and as a young lion to the house of Judah: I, even I, will tear and go away; I will take away, and none shall rescue him. 15 I will go and return to my place, till they are requited and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

5.10.1.en: These general disciplines revealed the sickness of Israel and the wounds of Judah, and it was fitting for them to turn to God in repentance, but Israel resorted to Assyria to support it [13], and behold, Assyria and its men were “miserable comforters” (Job 16:2) and “physicians of no value” (Job 13:4), and instead of supporting them they distressed them (2 Chr 28:16, 18). And since Israel did not benefit from the discipline, it came under a harsher and more bitter discipline, so we do not see God toward it as the moth or the woodworm but as the lion and the young lion. And in all this God hopes for its return: “I, even I, will tear and go away; I will take away, and none shall rescue him. I will go and return to my place, till they pass over and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early” [14-15].

5.10.2.en: What does He mean by saying, “I will return to my place”? Perhaps He wanted to make clear that in moments of discipline or the punishment of the wicked He is like one who “cometh out of his place” (Isa 26:21), appearing as one who is harsh, while His return to His place means His longing to declare His love for them and His accompaniment of them.

5.10.3.en: Finally, affliction makes the soul seek God early, therefore the Apostle advises us: “Is any among you afflicted? let him pray” (Jas 5:13). As Fr. John of Kronstadt says: [Often we draw near to God in time of distress, when no one but God can deliver us from it, and we return to Him with all our hearts… whereas in times of ease and abundance we leave God, especially when man thirsts for wealth and glory and distinction above others, for when he obtains these things he loses his faith from his heart and forgets God his Judge who will recompense him, forgets the immortality of his soul and his obligation to love God with all his heart and his neighbor as himself.]

6.0.0.en: 1 Come, and let us return unto the LORD: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up. 2 After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight. 3 Let us know, let us follow on to know the LORD. His going forth is sure as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter rain that watereth the earth.

6.0.1.en: When God tightens the noose on His fallen children, they seek Him early (Hos 5:15), saying: “Come, and let us return unto the LORD: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up” [1]. If He is like a lion that tears, it is only to heal us; if He smites, it is only to bind up our brokenness. As St. John Chrysostom wrote to a young widow wounded by the death of her husband at the hand of God, who permitted her this trial, saying: [Now I offer you this letter to be the first and greatest witness of God’s care for you, so that grief may not swallow you up, and your natural thoughts may not tear you down, when these troubles suddenly work to distress you… For it is said, “he hath torn, and he will heal us” [2], “he will smite us and bind up our wounds and heal us”… Now God has taken your husband to Himself, so He takes his place for you!] If His hand firmly holds the scalpel to wound, it is in truth uncovering our depths that bear the smell of death and corruption, and His hand remains stretched out to dress the wounds and grant us resurrection from the death in which we are; therefore He says: “After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live with him” [2].

6.0.2.en: He had said before: “in their affliction they will seek me early” (Hos 5:15), as though they stand early before the Lord Christ risen from the dead to find in His resurrection their own resurrection from among the dead. Truly it is fitting for us to enter with Him into His holy tomb, and to be buried with Him for “two days,” so that He may raise us on the third day and we may live before Him bearing His traits in us. We no longer fear the tomb as long as we are members of the body of the Lord Christ, which will not see corruption and which death cannot hold.

6.0.3.en: Thus the prophet saw, more than 700 years before the coming of the Lord Christ, in the resurrection of the Lord from the dead the secret of spiritual power… “we shall rise with him,” “we shall live with him,” “we shall know the Lord” [1-2]. By His resurrection we enjoy the good life that has become ours in Him, that is, the heavenly, exalted life, and by this we come to know the Lord. It is as though we enjoy what the two disciples of Emmaus obtained, those whom the Lord Christ, risen from the dead, accompanied, and as He spoke with them their hearts burned within them with His love and their inner sight was opened and they knew Him, saying to one another: “Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” (Lk 24:32).

6.1.0.en: Hosea, in the spirit of prophecy, presented to us the time of His resurrection, namely the dawn of the third day, for he says: “in the third day he will raise us up… His going forth is sure as the morning” [3]. The Church has been accustomed since the apostolic age to remember His resurrection constantly, especially in the Prime prayer, at dawn, the time of His resurrection, and as St. Cyprian says: [We must also pray in the morning, so that we celebrate by it the resurrection of the Lord]

6.1.1.en: The Lord rose at the dawn of the third day, to raise us at the dawn of our spiritual life; when we seek Him in us, He declares the power of His resurrection in our lives continually.

6.1.2.en: Perhaps his saying, “His going forth is sure as the morning,” means the certainty and assurance of His going forth, dispelling the darkness. The Septuagint reads: “we shall find him ready as the morning,” and as St. Augustine says, God is always present even if we do not perceive Him, “He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not” (Jn 1:10); when we return to Him He returns to us (Zech 1:3). And as St. John Chrysostom says: [The prophet points to the constant readiness of His goodness… for when we draw near to Him we find Him awaiting our movement.]

6.1.3.en: After announcing the resurrection of the Lord at the dawn of the third day, the secret of our salvation, he presents to us the work of the Holy Spirit, who was given to us later, “in the fullness of time,” after the ascension of the Lord Christ, for he says: “and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter rain that watereth the earth.” His Holy Spirit comes to us, descending upon us like the rain to transform us from dryness into a joyful garden, bearing the fruit of the Spirit that gladdens the heart of the Father, and the soul hears the whisper of her Bridegroom to her: “A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse” (Song 4:12).

6.1.4.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome sees in this rain a reference to the Lord Christ Himself, for he speaks in a discourse on the Holy Theophany (the Epiphany) of the dignity of the waters into which the Lord Christ entered and with which He was covered: [As for the water, there is something greater than all, namely the fact that Christ the Creator of all came down like the rain (Hos 6:3), and was known as the fountain (Jn 4:14), and was poured out as a river (Jn 7:38), and was baptized in the Jordan (Mt 3:13)… How wonderful that He is immersed in a little water, He who is the boundless river (Ps 46:4) which makes glad the city of God! The unfailing fountain, who bears life for all mankind, is covered by poor and temporary waters, He who is without end! He who is present in every place and is not absent from any place, whom the angels cannot comprehend and whom men cannot look upon, comes to Baptism according to His good pleasure.]

6.2.0.en: 4 “O Ephraim, what shall I do unto thee? O Judah, what shall I do unto thee? for your goodness is as a morning cloud, and as the early dew it goeth away. 5 Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and the judgment upon thee is as the light that goeth forth. 6 For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. 7 But they like Adam have transgressed the covenant: there have they dealt treacherously against me. 8 Gilead is a city of them that work iniquity, and is trodden with blood. 9 And as troops of robbers wait for a man, so the company of priests murder in the way toward Shechem: for they have committed lewdness. 10 I have seen an horrible thing in the house of Israel: there is the whoredom of Ephraim, Israel is defiled. 11 Also, O Judah, he hath set an harvest for thee, when I returned the captivity of my people.”

6.2.1.en: God Himself is the Savior; He rises from the dead to raise us with Him, and gives us His Holy Spirit as a latter rain that removes our dryness, giving His fruits in us, and not from ourselves. Therefore He says: “O Ephraim, what shall I do unto thee? O Judah, what shall I do unto thee? for your goodness (your righteousness) is as a morning cloud, and as the early dew it goeth away” [4]. Ephraim and Judah forgot their God and thought they were able to attain righteousness or goodness by their own work, and behold, this righteousness is like the morning cloud or the dew, unable to stand before the sun of trials. It is as though God says to them: What shall I do to you? For my part I have offered you my resurrection as the secret of your resurrection and given you my Holy Spirit to water your hearts, so why do you deprive yourselves of these my gifts, relying on your own righteousness, which is like the morning cloud and like the dew that quickly passes away?! And as St. John Chrysostom declares on the lips of the Lord: [He means this: for my part I offered everything indeed, but the hot sun comes upon you and scatters the cloud and the dew and makes them as nothing; therefore it is your evil that deprives you of my unspeakable goodness.]

6.3.0.en: The Lord continues His speech with them: “Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and the judges upon thee are as the light that goeth forth” [5]. And in the Septuagint: “Therefore I will reap (cut) your prophets, I will slay them by the words of my mouth…” They leaned on the false prophets who quieted their consciences with sweet, false words; therefore God disciplines these wicked men, and His judgment is like a slayer to them and like a light that exposes their darkness. As it is said: “he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked” (Isa 11:4).

6.3.1.en: If the words of God are life-giving, they are also deadly to evil and death, for the Lord by His words removes the deceit that is in the heart and kills it, shattering every darkness within us so that His judgment may appear as light in us. He is the one who shatters evil to build virtue, and scatters darkness so as to shine with His light in us.

6.4.0.en: Man cannot bring about inner reform of the heart… He can indeed offer sacrifices and burnt offerings and gifts and outward shows of devotion, but who is it that gives mercy and love and the knowledge of God and faithfulness in the covenant?! Therefore He says: “For I desired mercy (steadfast love), and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. But they like Adam have transgressed the covenant: there have they dealt treacherously against me” [6-7]. He wants inner works and a change of heart, which they cannot do from themselves, but it is the work of God Himself.

6.4.1.en: God is the one who works in us to grant us “mercy” or “steadfast love” in us, which gladdens His heart. The message of the Lord Christ came focusing on offering a change of our hard nature into the likeness of His nature, full of tenderness and love, so that we bear His traits in us.

6.4.2.en: St. John Chrysostom speaks to us about this mercy that God seeks in us, saying: [Now is not the time for judgment but for mercy; it is not for us to demand an account but to show love, it is not for us to bring suits but to waive them; it is not a time for judging and revenge, but to show mercy and do good.] This mercy is the nature of God Himself, as St. Ambrose writes in his treatise “On Repentance” against the followers of Novatian, who close the doors of God’s mercies before those who commit certain sins, saying: [We must know that God is a God of mercy, inclined to pardon and not to harshness. Therefore it is said: “I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.” How then does God accept your gifts, you who deny mercy, when it has been said of God that He has no pleasure in the death of the sinner, as that he should return (Ezek 18:32)?]

6.4.3.en: Through this divine mercy which we bear within us we come to know God, a knowledge of sharing His traits, which is what the Lord wants in us… “I desire… the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.” By this we bear within us faithfulness to the covenant made between God and us, and we are not counted as transgressors of it and traitors to it.

6.5.0.en: Let our reform be divine within, so that it may not be said of us: “But they like Adam have transgressed the covenant: there have they dealt treacherously against me. Gilead is a city of them that work iniquity, and is trodden with blood” [8]. May we not be like Adam, who transgressed the divine covenant while in the Paradise which God had set up for him, and so was counted a traitor to his Creator; may we enjoy His gifts and not deny His person. May we not be like Gilead, the city of them that work iniquity, trodden with blood, which is most likely the city of Ramoth-gilead, one of the three cities of refuge across the Jordan, a city of the Levites, containing men of the holy tribe, yet they were doers of evil who defiled themselves with blood through injustice and corruption. They had the appearance of piety and worship as Levites while in their depths they were wicked. May we also not be like the company of priests who put on the splendid vestments of the priesthood and practice worship in its outward formalities without life within, but within them is robbery, for He says: “And as troops of robbers wait for a man, so the company of priests murder in the way toward Shechem: for they have committed lewdness” [9]. Let us not be like them, who became robbers of souls, bearing a spirit of murder and destruction while concealed in priestly vestments, bringing ruin into the harbor of peace where people trust them.
